answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The vine multiplier is published, charged in saffron, and tide lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 3050 identities would post 2720 proofs and burn roughly 41 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
